_schema.description: Per-vendor/per-model MR scanner deliverability constants (gradient, RF, safety) with full citation provenance. Mirrors dmipy_sim biophysical_constants schema. Sections: 'scanners' (real machines, per model), 'envelopes' (declared limit points that are not a specific machine: the Pulseq presets and the Pulseq example system), 'classes' (the certificate's short names -> a scanners/envelopes key), 'aliases' (every other short name -> a key), 'safety'. Every scanner number in dmipy-sim is read from here; nothing in Python carries one.

confidence_levels.cited: value backed by a primary/authoritative source (vendor spec sheet, peer-reviewed methods paper, or IEC standard clause)
confidence_levels.widely-quoted: value is consistently reported but its primary authoritative source is unclear or coil/patient-dependent
confidence_levels.NEEDS VERIFICATION: no authoritative public source found; typically service-manual-confidential
confidence_levels.derived: value computed from a cited quantity (a slew rate from a stated rise time and amplitude); the derivation and its direction (a bound) are in context

b0_homogeneity.context: over a 16 cm DSV; the magnet is asymmetric in RL

background_gradient.context: the magnet's own field gradient at 8 cm from isocentre, up to 7 % of the diffusion gradient; it encodes diffusion alongside the pulsed gradient and the paper corrects ADC errors of up to 16.1 % with the b = 0 image

b0_quadratic.context: the even term c of dB/B0 = a x + c r^2 about isocentre: the isotropic bowl. Solved TOGETHER with b0_asymmetry_rl against both cited figures of this magnet, which it then reproduces exactly -- 1100 ppm peak-to-peak over the 16 cm DSV and a steepest 1.400 mT/m inside it. The two numbers determine the two coefficients between them: a purely linear field matching the DSV figure would need 0.44 mT/m rather than 1.4, and a purely isotropic one reaches only 80 % of the DSV figure, so the field needs both a bowl and a tilt
b0_quadratic.location: solved against the Methods' DSV homogeneity and the Appendix's background gradient

b0_validity_radius.context: how far from isocentre b0_quadratic is anchored: the radius the cited gradient was measured at. The law is an extrapolation beyond this and a consumer refuses rather than extrapolating

b0_asymmetry_rl.context: the ODD term a of dB/B0 = a x + c r^2, along the scanner's R/L axis: what 'the magnet is asymmetric in RL' means, and the term a bowl alone cannot express. A single yoke sits on one side, so the field is not mirror-symmetric about isocentre. It is substantial -- the field differs by 716 ppm between +8 and -8 cm, 1054 against 338 -- which is why an isotropic law is not good enough here. The SIGN is a convention: the source says the magnet is asymmetric but not which side is high, so +x (R) is assumed and a study that cares about the direction must check it
b0_asymmetry_rl.location: Methods, scanner description ('asymmetric in RL'); magnitude solved with b0_quadratic

hyperfine_swoop_64mT.notes: A permanent magnet's field follows its temperature, and this one is passively cooled with no temperature control over its cleared 15-30 degC range (510(k)). The measured coefficient is -1400 Hz/K = -514 ppm/K (ljungberg2025_unity, 244 scans at 17 sites) -- about HALF the bulk NdFeB figure, and what the machine is actually made of is not public. Two things keep that from reaching the data: the pre-scan calibration removes the between-session ambient term entirely, and the protocol re-centres f0 after every two DWIs (every volume, for royer2026_tract_64mT), attributing the within-scan drift to GRADIENT heating. (The 50 mT Halbach is the other way round -- there the gradients heat the magnet negligibly and the body is the source.) The gradients are passively cooled, which caps protocols near an hour. Its diffusion sequence is a non-CPMG SPLICE split-echo train (ohalloran2022_dwi_64mt).

b1_axial_falloff.context: the coefficient a of kappa_B1 = 1 - a z^2 about the coil's centre, z along the bore (superior-inferior). Derived from a measured B1+ map: 'little appreciable inhomogeneity in the transverse plane' and '15%-20% variation in the superior-inferior direction' over a 144 mm spherical phantom, so the fall-off is taken at the midpoint 17.5 % across the sphere's 72 mm half-extent. It is FLAT transversally, which is why this has no radial term -- the anisotropy is the citation's, not a simplification. A 180 degree pulse therefore delivers 148 degrees at the edge of that sphere
b1_axial_falloff.location: Results, Figure 3A-B (actual flip-angle imaging, 144 mm spherical phantom)

b1_calibration_offset.context: a SYSTEMATIC transmit scale, not a spatial one: 'the expected signal null at 180 degrees was consistently offset to 190 degrees, perhaps due to B1 errors', which is a scale of 190/180. It applies everywhere including isocentre, so it is separate from b1_axial_falloff and multiplies it. The same source reports a spread of about +/- 20 degrees around 300, i.e. +/- 6.7 %
b1_calibration_offset.location: Discussion, flip-angle sweep (1-420 degrees) on hardware v1.7

b1_load_independent.context: why a transmit profile is a property of the MACHINE at this field and may live in a scanner catalogue at all. At 2.7 MHz the RF wavelength in tissue is metres, so dielectric and standing-wave effects vanish: simulation across 47-100 mT in a 40-tissue head model finds 'only a 3% spatial variation between the maps obtained at 47 mT and 100 mT' while tissue permittivity changes by about 30 %. This value is that 3 %. The same claim must NOT be extended to 3 T or 7 T, where the profile is substantially the subject's
b1_load_independent.location: Results, normalized difference maps across 47/63.5/75/100 mT

f0_temperature_slope.context: how far the centre frequency moves per kelvin of ambient temperature, as PUBLISHED: a slope of -0.0014 MHz/degC from a linear mixed-effects regression of the DICOM centre frequency on phantom temperature over 244 scans at 17 sites, with site as a random effect (the sites differ in baseline frequency but not in slope). This is the only measured temperature coefficient of THIS machine. Its scope is narrow and matters: it is an AMBIENT sensitivity BETWEEN sessions over 18-24.5 degC, not a within-scan drift rate, and the phantom thermometer was discrete vials about a kelvin apart and censored at 24.5 degC, so the slope is more likely biased toward zero than away from it

b0_temperature_coefficient.context: the same measured slope as a fraction of B0: -1400 Hz / 2.725 MHz = -514 ppm/K. Divided out here rather than in a consumer, because the published figure is in hertz and the field law is a fraction. Worth knowing that this is about HALF the bulk NdFeB remanence coefficient (-0.09 to -0.12 %/K, quoted as ~-0.1 %/K by cooley2021_portable and measured as 2.5 kHz/degC at 50 mT by oreilly2021_halbach): the magnet is not all permanent-magnet material -- a steel yoke captures part of the flux and its permeability has a different, smaller temperature dependence. So the materials constant OVERSTATES this machine by a factor of two, and the measured figure is the one to use. Note also that no public document states what the Swoop's magnet is MADE of; the FDA filings and the specification sheet say only 'permanent magnet', and NdFeB appears in Hyperfine's patent US11215685B2 only as an example alongside SmCo, which is explicitly offered as the lower-drift alternative. At 514 ppm/K it takes about 2.1 K to equal this magnet's whole 1100 ppm spatial inhomogeneity
b0_temperature_coefficient.location: derived from the Results slope at f0 = gamma_bar x 0.064 T = 2.7249 MHz

operating_temperature_span.context: the width of the ambient range the scanner is cleared for, 15-30 degC, over which it has NO temperature control and no humidity control -- the 510(k) comparison table says so in as many words, alongside 'warm up time < 3 minutes' and no helium. The span matters because the magnet is uncontrolled across it: at the measured 514 ppm/K the two ends of the cleared range are 7700 ppm apart, 21 kHz, which is why the centre frequency is a calibration and never an assumption. The between-session ambient spread is in practice the LARGEST thermal term -- the UNITY sites span 18 to over 24.5 degC and many sit in unregulated rooms -- and it is entirely removed by the pre-scan calibration, which is why it never reaches the data
operating_temperature_span.location: technological characteristics comparison table, Operation Temperature / Temperature Control

f0_recentering_interval.context: how long the field is left to drift before the centre frequency is re-set: the Swoop's diffusion protocol re-centres f0 after every TWO DWIs following a short calibration scan, 'to account for B0 drift induced by gradient heating'. Two volumes of 212 shots at TR 800 ms is 339 s. This is what makes drift a small effect rather than a large one -- the accumulated offset is discarded and only what accrues within the interval reaches the data. It is an UPPER bound on current practice: a second group re-centres between every diffusion volume (royer2026_tract_64mT), which halves it. NO within-scan drift RATE is published for this machine. The nearest analogues are 50 mT Halbach systems at 800-1300 Hz/h, which is 0.32-0.52 K/h at their own 2.5 kHz/K; carried over at the Swoop's measured 1400 Hz/K that is 450-730 Hz/h, so 42-69 Hz within this interval. That is an estimate from another magnet's warming rate, not a measurement of this one
f0_recentering_interval.location: Methods, diffusion acquisition; the shot count and TR from ohalloran2022_dwi_64mt

local_extremities_first_level.context: First-Level Controlled Operating Mode, local SAR in extremities

partial_body_normal.context: Partial-body scales with exposed mass ratio r: SAR_limit = (10 - 8*r) W/kg in Normal mode

partial_body_first_level.context: Partial-body: SAR_limit = (10 - 6*r) W/kg in First-Level Controlled mode

second_level_controlled.context: Second-Level Controlled mode: above First-Level limits, requires ethics/IRB approval; no fixed IEC numeric ceiling

temperature_derating.context: all SAR limits assume ambient <= 25 degC; derate by ~0.25 W/kg for each degC above 25 (see Fig 201.103, Table 201.104)

definition.context: B1+rms is the RMS of the B1+ field over a defined averaging period (commonly stated as 10 s); IEC 60601-2-33 mandates that B1+rms be a user-selectable/displayed output (MR Equipment Output Conditioning, MROC) so it can be matched to MR-Conditional implant labeling. It is patient-mass-independent. There is NO single fixed numeric IEC ceiling for B1+rms; the limit is set by the implant's MR-Conditional label.
definition.location: Clause 201.12.4.103 / FPO output display requirements; see also mriquestions B1+rms

basis.context: Gradient output (dB/dt) is limited so as not to exceed the peripheral-nerve-stimulation (PNS) threshold. IEC 60601-2-33 expresses the limit via the rheobase/chronaxie stimulation model: Normal mode <= 80% of mean PNS threshold; First-Level <= 100% of mean PNS threshold; cardiac stimulation must always be avoided (Fig 201.102).

pns_threshold_model.context: Annex AA gives the strength-duration (rheobase/chronaxie) PNS threshold formulation and the dB/dt response-value convolution model (Figs AA.3-AA.7).

architecture.context: SAFE = Stimulation Approximation by Filtering and Evaluation. The gradient G(t) is differentiated (dG/dt), then split into >=2 (optionally 3) parallel low-pass filter branches with time constants tau1, tau2 (tau3 optional), each rectified, weighted by scale factors a1,a2,a3 and summed to form Stim(t); stimulation predicted if Stim(t) > Stim_lim. Empirical, vendor-implemented as a dB/dt watchdog.

weight_constraint.context: the weighting scale factors are normalized: a1 + a2 + a3 = 1.0

time_constant_range.context: filter time constants stated to lie in the ~5..15 ms range in the abstract; the specific per-filter tau1/tau2/tau3 values and per-coil scale factors a1/a2/a3 are NOT published (vendor-calibrated per gradient coil).
time_constant_range.location: Hebrank & Gebhardt 2000, Results ('5..15 ms with a1+a2+a3 = 1.0')

coefficients.context: Exact SAFE tau and a coefficients per gradient coil are vendor-confidential; only the architecture and normalization are published.

example_coefficients.context: The REPRESENTATIVE example gradient system's SAFE coefficients (per axis: three RC time constants, their normalised weights a1+a2+a3 = 1, the stimulation limit and the gradient scale), as shipped with safe_pns_prediction and pypulseq. NOT any specific scanner's calibration -- those are vendor-confidential (see 'coefficients'). The SAFE solver lives in dmipy-design; this is the data it reads.
example_coefficients.location: example hardware file in the repository

max_amplitude.context: the PULSEQ_SYSTEMS 'clinical_typical' preset: a nominal clinical system, not a machine

the PULSEQ_SYSTEMS 'preclinical_bruker' preset: a nominal preclinical system, not a machine (the cited Bruker systems are bruker_bga_9s, bruker_bga_12s_hp, bruker_bga_6s, bruker_micro2_5, bruker_micro5)

rf_dead_time.context: RF dead time of the example system used by Pulseq exporters so check_timing is meaningful; no vendor spec sheet publishes one (the Prisma leaf is NEEDS VERIFICATION for that reason). Was hard-coded in dmipy-design pulseq_export._DEAD.

adc_dead_time.context: example-system ADC dead time, as rf_dead_time
